Definition: properly, entity; used only as a particle of affirmation, there is
BiblicalUsage: ʼIythay is the Aramaic word for 'there is' or 'there are,' the plain way of saying that something exists. Daniel uses it to tell Nebuchadnezzar there is a God in heaven who reveals secrets, and the three friends use it to say there is a God able to deliver them from the furnace.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that this little word matters because the whole question of the exile was whether there is a God in heaven who rules kings and rescues His people — and Daniel answers yes.
RelatedEvents: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego in the Fiery Furnace
